correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the computation in RESULT.md lines 31–53. In graph-state basis amplitudes, tracing the line register gives cancellation unless B_fault transposed annihilates the difference of the two point labels; the reduced density then has identical rank-one blocks indexed by the corresponding cosets, giving rank 2^rank(B_fault) and flat nonzero eigenvalues. Odd q gives BB^T=I+J and B1=B^T1=0 in F₂, with n odd, so B has corank one. For the matching update, z=V^Tx forces even parity by the left kernel. Every preimage of Uz is B^TUz+c1; asking it to have V^Tx=z gives exactly the bordered equations. The maps in both directions are inverse, including k=0. When D=0 and k≥1 the border imposes c=0 and one parity constraint, so the loss relative to pristine is k−2. With two flags one cross-incidence instead gives determinant 1 for K_F, while two cross-incidences violate uniqueness of the common line. For Desarguesian odd q the stated finite point/tangent dot product is (s−t)^2 and neither type of finite/infinite cross-incidence occurs; this works over all the specified fields. Read VERIFY.py, VERIFICATION.md and the supplied finite check output without executing the script. Those prime-order tests are not the basis for the general result.
